newsitem.title: HONG KONG: BA Asia signs pact for Indonesia project.
newsitem.headline: BA Asia signs pact for Indonesia project.

text.p: BA Asia, Bank of America's Hong Kong-based merchant banking unit, said it has signed a financial agreement to construct a US$2.3 billion petrochemicals plant in Indonesia.
The agreement is with PT Trans-Pacific Petrochemical Indotama (TPPI), an Indonesian petrochemical joint venture company, to construct an olefins and aromatics facility in Tuban, East Java.

The petrochemical complex will be the largest undertaking of its kind in Indonesia and will use primarily Indonesian condensate as feedstock to produce petrochemicals, which previously had been imported.
BA Asia said it is acting as the sole financial advisor to the project company and has provided an underwriting commitment for a significant portion of the debt.
As much as US$1.725 billion in project debt is expected to be raised from various export agencies, international commercial banks, Indonesian banks and Japanese trading companies.
Financial close is expected to take place in the third quarter of 1997, BA Asia said.

A shareholders agreement for the project has been entered into by PT Tirtamas (10 percent), its affiliate Trans Pacific Petrochemicals (60 percent), a subsidiary of Siam Cement Public Co (20 percent) and Nissho Iwai Corp (10 percent), BA Asia said.

A contractor consortium to construct the facilities also has been announced. The consortium comprises U.S.-based Stone and Webster Engineering Co, AFC International Projects Inc, Process Engineers Inc and Japan's JGC Corp.

TPPI also expects to sign an agreement with Koch Refining Pte Ltd, a subsidiary of U.S.-based Koch Industries, to supply additional condensate for the project and to purchase, on a standby-basis, excess aromatic products produced.

The project will have the capacity to produce three million metric tons per annum of olefins, aromatics and other products. It is expected to use 98,000 barrels per stream day of condensate as feedstock, BA Asia said.

The majority of the olefins and a portion of the aromatics produced will be sold to downstream petrochemical facilities. All facilities will be constructed simultaneously and collectively comprise the Tuban petrochemical complex.
Shareholder Nissho Iwai on Friday pegged the total value of the Tuban project, including the portion that has been signed and the parts still under negotiation, at US$3.1 billion.
